utterances.speaker: RAMIZ SUBASIC
utterances.text: I'm not going to go into that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please let us see the last page of this document now. I think it's page 20.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Sir, have a look at the penultimate paragraph. It is the same in the English and B/C/S versions. It says, and it is a report on finger-print analysis carried out in accordance with the request mentioned on the previous page which I showed you, and this is what it says: "The questioned print taken from the body found in the Vrbas River marked as number 2," it is the first document that I showed you, "was identical to the control print of the right index finger on the personal identity card of Dedo Crnalic, son of Dervis and Razija ... born on the 15th of October, 1926, in Prijedor." Is that what it says, sir?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ SUBASIC
utterances.text: That's what it says. But whether it's correct, that's what we don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Sir, on the basis of what I read out to you, it follows that you are not telling the truth.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ SUBASIC
utterances.text: I believe that this document is not truthful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I suppose what the witness said before I could complete my observation was inevitable. Mr. Aleksic, that's an argument.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: I agree with you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: We see the path that you have laid out through this document, so we have that on the one hand and the witness's testimony on the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I say something? Your Honours, thank you. I have understood. I have no more questions for this witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ SUBASIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I'll be much briefer. Mr. Dedo Crnalic died as a result of the beating he received along the way at one of the stops and was not alive at the moment of the bus's arrival in front of Manjaca. Is what I just said true?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ SUBASIC
utterances.text: I don't think so. I'm not the only person who saw it happen at Manjaca. I could bring in a number of witnesses who would say the same thing as I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: What witnesses?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ SUBASIC
utterances.text: It is irrelevant now, but if there's anything in dispute, I could tell you. I don't know, though, whether they would like to remain anonymous.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you specifically about Mr. Murselovic. Do you know the owner of Cafe Mursel?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ SUBASIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Was he in Manjaca? Did he arrive on the same transport?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ SUBASIC
utterances.text: I didn't see him, but I think he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Very well. I will put forth another assertion. The late Dedo Crnalic was executed by firing squad at Manjaca; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ SUBASIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat his answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: The interpreters are asking you to repeat your last answer.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ SUBASIC
utterances.text: I didn't see that, and I don't know if it's true or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: How come you don't know, when you have a completely different story? Then you know it's not true.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ SUBASIC
utterances.text: I stand by what I said. I won't go into what you are talking about. I'm not interested.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm asking you whether he was executed by firing squad.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ SUBASIC
utterances.text: I don't know that. I couldn't see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Cvijetic, I -- do I correctly assume that you are not merely trying to provoke an argument with the witness but that this is evidence that you intend to bring at some -- at some point, because my recollection is that this is the first time we're hearing about this assertion. As I said, if it's something you intend to lead evidence on positively later, but if at this point you're just throwing out theories, I don't know how useful that is, or correct, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, there seem to be a disconjunction between the two Defence counsel here, because at one point Defence counsel is claiming that this witness had only been beaten and that they have an exhumation report to that effect, and now this Defence counsel is arguing that he was shot. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: You needn't concern yourself with that aspect, Mr. Olmsted. That's a matter for the -- they would argue this at the end of the day. But, Mr. Cvijetic, I return to the admissibility of this line of questions if you, in fact, are not going to be in a position to positively lead evidence in support of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we are well in a position to do that, but the Prosecution and the Defence had a witness here testifying to that effect, and we had two statements I referred to that were used with another witness. We now have a third version of Mr. Crnalic's death, and I'm now simply putting forth to this witness the two previous stories of his death that we have already heard before this Chamber, if you recall. If needed, I can tell you what evidence, specifically, I have in mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Cvijetic, can we have the pseudonym of the witness you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He testified publicly. It was not a protected witness. I can state his first and last name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I just want the pseudonym, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] ST-227.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Did he -- did he testify that Mr. Crnalic was executed by a firing squad?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, that witness was shown his statement he provided to the court in Sanski Most as part of the proceedings undertaken to declare Mr. Dedo Crnalic officially dead, and that was the version that witness offered to the Court. We faced him with that document. In front of you he said that he had been beaten and that by the time he arrived in front of Manjaca he had been dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is misstating the evidence of the prior witness, and I don't think the Defence counsel should go any further on that. There was a document shown to a prior witness that suggested that this particular victim was shot, and that witness clearly said that he never made that -- such a statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm merely trying to verify which of the three versions is correct. Otherwise, I have no further questions of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Just one question.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. It will be -- it will be very quickly, the question I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Sir, you mentioned that when you saw Mr. Crnalic that morning before he was called away by Babic and Mrdja, he appeared in very poor condition, could hardly walk. Can you go into a little more detail about that? Did it appear that he had been recently beaten?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ SUBASIC
utterances.text: Yes, he did. That's what he looked like. He was all broken up.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: No further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, you told us that when -- at the killing of Mr. Crnalic there were active police officers outside the gate present; right? That's what you said to us.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ SUBASIC
utterances.text: They were present, but the murder was carried out by the members of the Intervention Platoon, Mr. Mrdja and Mr. Babic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Did the active police officers witness this killing?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ SUBASIC
utterances.text: They did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Did they react in any way?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ SUBASIC
utterances.text: No. No one dared disturb the two in the act. I think they were the ones who had the final say as some sort of heroes or leaders.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. One last question. You -- well, we have go into private session for just one moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Sir, we thank you for your willingness to relive these horrific experiences and to assist the Tribunal. You are now released, and we wish you a safe journey back to your home. The usher will escort you from the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Olmsted, does the Prosecution have further witnesses it intends to lead today?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Unfortunately, no, Your Honours. The witnesses that we had originally scheduled to follow this witness we've rescheduled them for Monday because earlier this week we did not believe, given the amount of cross-examination anticipated, that they would have testified this week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. In that case, we now take the adjournment to -- and I believe we are back in this courtroom, and it's Monday morning. I trust everyone has a safe weekend. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 18th day of October, 2010, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 12.13 p.m.,
